answer.text: An external (tape) merge-sort strategy that uses P tapes but merges P−1 inputs into one output, rotating roles

feedback.text: Correct — it keeps one output tape and merges from the other P−1, then rotates.

answer.text: An in-memory variant of quicksort using multiple pivots

feedback.text: No — polyphase is an external merge strategy, unrelated to pivots.

answer.text: A hashing scheme for distributing keys across buckets

feedback.text: No — it merges sorted runs across tapes; it is not hashing.

answer.text: A stable counting sort for small integer keys

feedback.text: No — that describes counting sort, not polyphase merge.

generalfeedback.text: Polyphase merge sort distributes runs over P tapes and repeatedly does (P−1)-way merges into one output, rotating which tape is the output.

questiontext.text: How are the initial runs distributed across the tapes so the merges stay "perfect" (no idle passes)?

answer.text: In a (generalized) Fibonacci proportion

feedback.text: Correct — Fibonacci-numbered counts keep every merge phase perfectly balanced.

answer.text: Split exactly evenly across all tapes

feedback.text: No — an even split is balanced merge, not polyphase; it wastes rewind passes.

answer.text: All runs placed on a single tape

feedback.text: No — the merges need runs spread over P−1 input tapes.

answer.text: In powers of two on two tapes

feedback.text: No — the distribution follows Fibonacci-like numbers, not simple powers of two.

generalfeedback.text: Choosing run counts as consecutive (generalized) Fibonacci numbers lets each phase merge without leaving a tape idle.

questiontext.text: What is the main advantage of polyphase merge over balanced k-way merge?

answer.text: It achieves comparable performance with fewer tapes and avoids full rewind/copy passes

feedback.text: Correct — clever distribution replaces the balanced method's idle rewind/redistribution passes.

answer.text: It removes the need to compare keys at all

feedback.text: No — it still compares keys during each merge.

answer.text: It makes the sort run in O(n) time

feedback.text: No — it is still an O(n log n)-work merge sort; the win is fewer tape passes.

answer.text: It requires no initial run creation phase

feedback.text: No — it still starts by creating sorted runs.

generalfeedback.text: Balanced merge needs an even split and wastes rewind/redistribution passes; polyphase trades a Fibonacci distribution for fewer tapes and fewer total passes.

questiontext.text: In polyphase merge sort, each phase merges from P−1 input tapes onto a single output tape, and the roles of the tapes rotate between phases.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — one output, P−1 inputs, and the output role rotates each phase.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: No — this rotating single-output scheme is exactly how polyphase works.

questiontext.text: Polyphase merge sort requires the initial runs to be distributed equally across all the tapes.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: No — it uses an uneven, Fibonacci-like distribution, not an equal split.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — the runs follow a (generalized) Fibonacci distribution, not an even one.

questiontext.text: The number sequence whose values give the ideal initial run counts for polyphase merge is the ______ sequence.

answer.text: Fibonacci

feedback.text: Correct — (generalized) Fibonacci numbers.

answer.text: Fibonacci*

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: *Fibonacci*

feedback.text: Correct — generalized Fibonacci also accepted.

questiontext.text: Polyphase merge sort was historically important for which storage technology?

answer.text: Magnetic tape drives, where the number of tapes and rewinds mattered

feedback.text: Correct — minimizing tapes and rewind passes was crucial on tape systems.

answer.text: CPU registers

feedback.text: No — it is about external, sequential storage, not registers.

answer.text: Content-addressable memory

feedback.text: No — the motivation was sequential tape access, not associative memory.

answer.text: GPU shared memory

feedback.text: No — polyphase predates and is unrelated to GPU memory.

generalfeedback.text: On tape drives, having few tapes and avoiding rewind/copy passes was vital, which is exactly what polyphase optimizes.

questiontext.text: Which statements about polyphase merge sort are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: It uses P tapes but merges only P−1 of them at a time into one output

feedback.text: Yes — one tape is the output while P−1 serve as inputs.

answer.text: Initial runs are distributed in (generalized) Fibonacci counts to keep merges perfect

feedback.text: Yes — the Fibonacci distribution avoids idle passes.

answer.text: It splits the runs evenly like balanced merge

feedback.text: No — an even split is balanced merge; polyphase is deliberately uneven.

answer.text: It eliminates the initial run-creation phase entirely

feedback.text: No — sorted runs must still be created first.

generalfeedback.text: Polyphase = P tapes, (P−1)-way rotating merges, Fibonacci run distribution; it still needs run creation and is not an even split.
